scene_scripts.narrator_film_candidate: Six separate confrontations, one Commonwealth, and four games still to come. The record says what happened. The roads tell us what it cost.
scene_scripts.camera_action_direction: Travel a sealed folio, winding route markers, and recognizable props with one continuous oblique table move. Stop on the empty space waiting for Week Eleven.
scene_scripts.source_unchanged_body: Two teams crossed two hundred by Sunday night. One brought a hamburger to a birthday party. The other left his chair and offered a man a bargain on his own mountain. In the Highlands, an outlaw got his laugh, copied a centaur’s stance for a second one, and gave the centaur a reason to chase him. In the east, El Niño’s rain found a way past Red Leopards’ sandbags. Inland, trees were already coming down. Seven Deadly Chins arrived with a jackhammer just as a household settled. Slob on my Dobb kept a delivery appointment in a swamp. Four regular-season games remain. Who has to live with what happened here?

scene_scripts.narrator_film_candidate: The standings will be entered once. A fallen hoop stays fallen. A truck passes the same empty road every week. The people in this world have to live with both truths.
scene_scripts.camera_action_direction: An anonymous official seals the weather-worn door. Keep civic labor ordinary, no commissioner portrait, no unverified speech.
scene_scripts.source_unchanged_body: There is a difference between being beaten and having to live with the evidence. A score is entered once. A birthday photograph is shown forever. A broken hoop stays broken until someone fixes it. The owner of a swamp still has to watch the next truck drive through. That is the Commonwealth we have spent seasons building, and it is why this league is more than six boxes on a scoreboard. But our stories do not outrank the standings. Nobody is going to Cancún by mathematical decree until the last route is closed. Nobody is healed because a reserve slot looks full. The numbers have settled, and six teams now share 6–4 records. The next week will ask each of us what we have left to field.
